# Lab 5.7: Apache Spark Stored Procedures

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a Spark connection and a PySpark stored procedure that reads a BigQuery table, aggregates it, and writes the result back, all called from SQL.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Create a Spark connection.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq mk --connection --connection_type='SPARK' --location=US lab_spark
SPARK_SA=$(bq show --format=json --connection $PROJECT_ID.us.lab_spark | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['spark']['serviceAccountId'])")
echo $SPARK_SA
for ROLE in roles/bigquery.dataEditor roles/bigquery.jobUser roles/bigquery.readSessionUser; do
  gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID --member=serviceAccount:$SPARK_SA --role=$ROLE --quiet
done</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Create the procedure.** Replace `YOUR_PROJECT`.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE lab05.spark_corpus_counts()
WITH CONNECTION `YOUR_PROJECT.us.lab_spark`
OPTIONS (engine = 'SPARK')
LANGUAGE PYTHON AS R"""
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("corpus-counts").getOrCreate()
df = spark.read.format("bigquery").load("bigquery-public-data.samples.shakespeare")
out = df.groupBy("corpus").agg(F.sum("word_count").alias("words"))
out.write.format("bigquery").option("writeMethod", "direct").mode("overwrite").save("lab05.spark_corpus_counts")
""";</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Run it.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">

<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CALL lab05.spark_corpus_counts();
SELECT * FROM lab05.spark_corpus_counts ORDER BY words DESC LIMIT 5;</span>

   The first call takes a minute or two while serverless Spark starts.

4. **[Console] Look at the Spark logs.** In the job's **Execution details**, click the link to the Spark batch logs.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Connection | `us.lab_spark` with its own service account |
| Procedure | PySpark code stored in BigQuery |
| Engine | Serverless Spark, no cluster to manage |
| Output | `spark_corpus_counts` table |
